subject: Clarification: SOC 2 coverage window & EU/UK hosting boundary for FinTrust POC
messages:
From: Emma Harris <emma.harris@fintrust.co.uk>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintrust.co.uk
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: SOC2 Type II coverage & hosting boundary for Redwood (FinTrust POC)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Procurement/security have a few gating items before we can proceed to contract: they asked me to collect the following from Redwood:

- Copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted is fine) that covers at least 2026 calendar year (Jan 1 2026 - Dec 31 2026).
- If the active report period doesn't fully cover our requested window (Jan 2026 - Mar 2027), a signed bridge letter attesting controls continuity and any exceptions.
- A clear hosting boundary statement for our EU tenant: we need to know whether customer data (including backups, logs, and metadata) stays in EU-only infrastructure and whether any part of the control plane, telemetry, or backups transit or are processed in the US/other regions.
- SIG/CAIQ or evidence mapping if available (or a pointer to where to retrieve).

I attached a short checklist used by our vendor team (FINTRUST_SOC2_REQ_v3.pdf). Can you confirm what you can provide and the expected turnaround?

Thanks,
Emma Harris
Head of Vendor Risk — FinTrust Bank
emma.harris@fintrust.co.uk
Phone: +44 20 7946 0xxx

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Harris <emma.harris@fintrust.co.uk>
Cc: security@fintrust.co.uk
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II coverage & hosting boundary for Redwood (FinTrust POC)

Hi Emma,

Thanks for the checklist — appreciate the clarity. Quick summary of what we can provide and next steps: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report: we can provide a redacted copy of our 2026 SOC 2 Type II report (covers controls through 2026-12-31). I will attach a redacted PDF for immediate review and can provide a full copy under NDA if needed.

2) Bridge letter: if you need confirmation that controls remained in place into 2027 Q1, we can issue a signed bridge letter. Ive attached our bridge-letter template for reference and Marissa (legal/compliance) will finalize language. Typical turnaround is 3-5 business days after we agree on the period and signing approach.

3) Hosting boundary: for hosted Redwood API customers with an EU tenant, the data plane (model inference, token payloads, ephemeral cache and customer-controlled storage like embeddings) is deployed in EU regions (we use eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for EU tenants). Control plane metadata (orchestration/management plane) may be hosted in a separate control region — for many customers this is in our control plane in the US. Backups and long‑term artifact storage are configurable per-customer and can be restricted to EU-only when required (we can provide evidence/config settings).

4) Evidence mapping & CAIQ: we maintain a SIG/CAIQ mapping and a short dataflow diagram that shows where logs, backups, and telemetry land. I will upload the CAIQ/SIG export and the diagram to a shared Drive link and flag the relevant sections.

Next steps: can you confirm whether FinTrust requires all control plane services to be EU-only (some banks do) or whether control plane/management metadata in the US is acceptable provided data plane and backups remain in EU? That will determine whether we need to propose a Private deployment or apply additional contractual assurances (SCCs / DPA language \u2013 if needed we can also discuss a hybrid model).

Ive looped in Marissa (cc) for the bridge letter and Rishi for technical evidence (IP ranges, S3 regions, KMS).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Product Security (Solutions) — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Harris <emma.harris@fintrust.co.uk>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintrust.co.uk
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II coverage & hosting boundary for Redwood (FinTrust POC)

Emma — thanks for the checklist. A few clarifications from legal/compliance: 

- Attached: redwood-bridge-letter-template.docx (editable) and redwood-soc2-2026-redacted.pdf (redacted). The bridge letter template includes an attestation period field ")from"/"to" that we will populate for your requested window.
- We typically sign bridge letters on company letterhead and can include the scope (services covered) and the audit firm name.
- If you need a formal DPA addendum or SCCs referenced explicitly in the letter, please flag which clauses are required and we will route to our legal team.

Proposed timeline: once you confirm the exact audit window you want covered, we will:
  1) Draft the bridge letter (1 business day)
  2) Internal signoff (1-2 business days)
  3) Return signed PDF to you

If FinTrust requires a control-plane residency guarantee (control plane in EU), that typically moves to our Private deployment offering; we can include a separate proposal from Sales for that.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs:
- redwood-bridge-letter-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Harris <emma.harris@fintrust.co.uk>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintrust.co.uk
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:27:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II coverage & hosting boundary for Redwood (FinTrust POC)

Hi Emma — adding technical detail to Sofia/Marissa's notes so your engineers/vendor risk team can map controls to the checklist you sent: 

- Data plane / inference: for EU tenants, inference hosts (GPU instances), ephemeral KV cache, and transient token state are pinned to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. We do not route inference payloads through US regions for EU tenants.

- Backups & long-term artifacts: customer-configurable. For EU-only customers we configure S3 buckets in eu-west-1. Backups are encrypted with customer‑scoped KMS keys; keys can be provisioned in the customer's KMS or our managed KMS in the EU.

- Control plane: orchestration APIs, telemetry ingestion, and some operational metadata live in our global control plane (primary cluster in us-east-1). The control plane stores only operational metadata (instance identifiers, routing state) and does not contain plaintext customer prompt data or model input/outputs. Where customers require, we offer Private deployment (control plane and data plane fully in-customer VPC) or a dedicated control plane residency arrangement.

- Network egress & cross-border flow: we publish IP ranges for EU endpoints and can provide a signed statement that no customer payloads are intentionally routed to non-EU data plane regions for EU tenants. Any incidental operational metadata replication to the US control plane is pseudonymized and encrypted; we can supply logs/traces for audit sampling on request.

- Evidence we can provide: IP range list, dataflow diagram (attached: dataflow-eu-uk-diagram.png), S3 region configuration screenshots, KMS key metadata (redacted), and a CAIQ/SIG export.

Let me know which items from the FINTRUST_SOC2_REQ_v3 checklist you want first (SOC 2 report redaction, bridge letter, IP ranges, config screenshots), and Ill prioritize.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
